title: sentAt field from peer not validated — accepts arbitrary timestamps
description: Peer/deliver accepts sentAt from the sending peer without validation. Per CLAUDE.md trust boundary table: 'Peer sentAt timestamp — Nothing — use receivedAt (local clock) for ordering. Sender clock is unverified.' The code stores sentAt as-is which allows peers to inject messages with arbitrary past/future timestamps that corrupt ordering. Fix: ignore peer-supplied sentAt and always use the local receivedAt clock for ordering.
